name: Libya
summary_text: Libya is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. The Penal Code criminalises “illicit sexual intercourse” and “indecent acts” (up to 5 years), and Cairo 52 documents de-facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition through these provisions — compounded by recent religious rulings declaring the very term “gender” haram, making anyone using it in media or institutions susceptible to prosecution. Militias control territory and operate detention sites where torture is systematic; there is no functioning central judiciary, no LGR, and no protection of any kind. For a visitor: detention by any of several militia authorities is the modal bad outcome, with no consular reach in much of the country.

sources.title: Libya | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Libya: de facto criminalisation of gender nonconformity and transition (social, medical, surgical) via 'indecent acts' and 'illicit intercourse' provisions; recent religious rulings designate the term 'gender' as haram, exposing users to punishment; no legal gender recognition framework or court attempts; armed militias retaliate against gender-diverse people amid the post-2011 conflict.

sources.title: Libya | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity criminalised (up to 5 years under 'illicit sexual intercourse' and 'indecent acts' provisions applying to men and women); no SOGISC protections; no legal gender recognition; enforcement and repression intensified after 2011 - armed groups and security agencies arrest people based on perceived orientation or gender identity, with discrimination, violence and arbitrary detention.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying Human Dignity Trust country profile documents Libya's criminalisation of same-sex activity.

sources.title: Everything you need to know about being gay in Muslim countries | LGBTQ+ rights | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (June 2016): Brian Whitaker's 'Everything you need to know about being gay in Muslim countries' - the official fiction is that gay people don't exist in the Middle East; family and societal attitudes are often a bigger problem than state persecution; Libya among the countries covered.

sources.title: Islamic State's War on Gays | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: HRW (June 2015): 'Islamic State's War on Gays' - documents ISIS executions of men accused of homosexuality in territories it controlled, including in Libya.

sources.title: Less than human
sources.claim_summary: D+C (June 2015): 'The situation for homosexuals in Libya is getting worse' - ISIS executed three young men in Derna (kneeling in plastic tubs, shot in the back of the head before a crowd); considered the first death sentence against homosexuals in modern Libya's history; no one in Derna dares speak of the killings.

sources.title: Libyan 'Gay' Men Face Torture, Death By Militia: Report (GRAPHIC) | HuffPost Voices
sources.claim_summary: HuffPost (Nov 2012): report that 12 men accused of being gay faced torture and death by a Libyan militia - NOTE: the original source was a Facebook page falsely claiming HRW affiliation, which later apologised for misrepresenting itself; treat with caution.
